A complementary Enrichr analysis provided complementary immune-related signals, although these did not remain significant after multiple-testing corrections. Malat1, Neat1, and Gas5 were selected for RT-qPCR validation and showed expression patterns consistent with sequencing. AlphaFold 3 predicted Snu13 as a potential interactor of the three candidate lncRNAs, providing a hypothesis for future experimental investigation but not establishing a role in exosomal RNA sorting. Overall, these findings provide a transcriptomic resource and computational framework for prioritizing exosomal lncRNAs associated with B. abortus infection and support further investigation of EV-associated lncRNA loading mechanism and their potential functional relevance.

title: Conditioned medium from Sanhuang Decoction-pretreated MDA-MB-231 cells attenuates endothelial inflammation and barrier dysfunction.
abstract: Tumor-cell-derived inflammatory signals can alter endothelial activation and barrier integrity in triple-negative breast cancer. Whether pretreating tumor cells with Sanhuang Decoction (SHD) changes the subsequent conditioned-medium (CM)-associated endothelial phenotype remains unclear. MDA-MB-231 cells were exposed to SHD, washed twice with phosphate-buffered saline, and cultured in fresh drug-free medium before CM collection. Tumor-cell migration, CXCL8 mRNA, and viable donor-cell-normalized CXCL8 secretion were assessed, with selected CCK-8 and CXCL8 validation in MDA-MB-468, BT-549, and Hs578T cells. Human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) were exposed to Control-CM, 231-CM, or CM from SHD-pretreated MDA-MB-231 cells and evaluated by RNA sequencing, RT-qPCR, western blotting, immunofluorescence, FITC-dextran permeability, CellTracker-based transendothelial migration, and representative transmission electron microscopy. A direct-SHD HUVEC western blot control and the PI3K agonist 740 Y-P were used to examine direct-exposure effects and pathway participation. Public-data, LC-HRMS/MS profiling, HPLC-DAD emodin marker analysis, network, and enrichment analyses provided study context. SHD reduced MDA-MB-231 migration, decreased CXCL8 mRNA across the TNBC validation panel, and reduced viable donor-cell-normalized CXCL8 secretion in all four TNBC cell lines, most consistently at 6 mg/mL. In HUVECs, SHD6-CM was associated with opposite-direction changes in a subset of 231-CM-associated transcriptomic features involving cytoskeletal, vascular-wall interaction, PI3K/AKT, and junction-related programs. It reduced VCAM-1, ICAM-1, and PI3K/AKT phosphorylation while increasing ZO-1, VE-cadherin, and Occludin-related readouts. Direct SHD exposure did not reproduce this coordinated HUVEC protein pattern. SHD6-CM was also associated with lower FITC-dextran permeability and fewer CellTracker Green-positive MDA-MB-231 cells crossing the endothelial monolayer. Addition of 740 Y-P attenuated these molecular and functional changes, consistent with partial PI3K/AKT participation. CM from SHD-pretreated MDA-MB-231 cells was associated with reduced endothelial inflammatory activation and improved barrier-related readouts in this in vitro model. CXCL8 remains an associated candidate mediator within a multicomponent secretory response, rather than an established sole mediator, and pathway-specific experiments are needed to define the contribution of PI3K/AKT.

title: Restoration of CD8+ T cell stress resilience and abscopal effect of radioimmunotherapy via SFRP2-WNT-HSF1 pathway targeting.
abstract: The abscopal effect, in which radiotherapy of one tumor is associated with regression of distant non-irradiated tumors, remains uncommon even when combined with immune checkpoint blockade. Although systemic T cell priming is required, the mechanisms that determine whether effector T cells persist within distant tumors remain unclear. We investigated whether SFRP2-expressing stromal cells limit CD8+ T cell stress resilience in abscopal tumors. We used bilateral mouse tumor models treated with fractionated radiotherapy plus anti-PD-1 antibody, combined with immune profiling of irradiated tumors, tumor-draining lymph nodes, and distant tumors. Human lung cancer specimens, public transcriptomic datasets, fibroblast-specific Sfrp2 deletion, single-cell RNA sequencing, immunostaining, flow cytometry, and fibroblast-T cell co-culture assays were used to examine the relationship between SFRP2, CD8+ T cell apoptosis, and stress-response signaling. Statistical analyses included two-sided tests and multiple-comparison correction where appropriate. Here we show that radioimmunotherapy activates local tumor immunity and tumor-draining lymph node priming, but resistant distant tumors fail to maintain CD8+ T cell accumulation. SFRP2 is enriched in fibroblast-like stromal compartments and is inversely associated with CD8+ T cell infiltration. Fibroblast-specific Sfrp2 deletion reduces CD8+ T cell apoptosis and restores an HSPA1A/HSP70-associated stress-resilience program. Mechanistically, SFRP2 suppresses a WNT-HSF1-HSPA1A signaling program, whereas Hspa1a overexpression reduces SFRP2-associated caspase-3 activation in T cells. These findings identify stromal suppression of CD8+ T cell stress resilience as a mechanism of abscopal resistance and support SFRP2-WNT-HSF1 pathway targeting as a potential strategy to improve radioimmunotherapy.

title: RAD51 and XRCC2 Genetics Variants and Multiple Myeloma Risk, Chromosomal Aberrations, and Clinical Outcomes.
abstract: Multiple myeloma (MM) is a hematologic malignancy characterized by genomic instability, frequently involving chromosomal translocations and deletions. Such abnormalities often result from DNA double-stranded breaks. RAD51 and XRCC2 gene products play key roles in the homologous recombination repair of these breaks. In this study, we investigated the role of selected genetic variants in MM pathogenesis and progression. Specifically, we analyzed two RAD51 polymorphisms (rs1801321 - 172G>T and rs1801320 - 135G>C) and one in XRCC2 (rs3218536 - Arg188His). The RAD51 variants are located in the 5' untranslated region and may affect gene regulation or expression, whereas the XRCC2 rs3218536 variant results in an amino acid substitution that may influence protein function. The study aimed to evaluate the associations between these variants and chromosomal aberrations (deletions/translocations), the risk of developing MM, and treatment response. Genomic DNA extracted from 117 newly diagnosed MM patients and 187 healthy blood donors was used to analyze RAD51 and XRCC2 variants (via real-time PCR). The method of cIg-FISH was applied for analysis of chromosomal aberrations. Gene-expression analysis was performed in 85 patient samples from which sufficient high-quality RNA was obtained from isolated CD138-positive plasma cells. The T allele of RAD51 rs1801321 was associated with a significantly reduced risk of MM (OR = 0.52, 95% CI: 0.37-0.73, p < 0.001). However, RAD51 rs1801320 and XRCC2 rs3218536 showed no association with MM susceptibility. None of the studied variants were found to correlate with chromosomal aberrations or overall survival. Exploratory analyses showed that the rs1801321 T allele and the RAD51 rs1801320 GG genotype were associated with higher XRCC2 expression. The RAD51 rs1801321 T allele was associated with lower MM susceptibility in the present cohort. However, RAD51 rs1801320 and XRCC2 rs3218536 do not appear to have a significant impact on chromosomal aberrations, disease progression or treatment response.

title: Drosha in mesangial cells regulates glomerular capillary tufts formation through drosha/ribosome/Gata3 axis.
abstract: Drosha is a critical regulator of kidney development; its loss or mutation, identified in a subset of Wilms tumor (WT), a pediatric kidney cancer, leads to nephric cap mesenchyme developmental defects. Here, we investigated the role of Drosha in mesangial cells and its impact on glomerular capillary tuft formation. Mesangial cells specific deletion of Drosha (Drosha cKO) in mouse model was generated. Deletion of Drosha in mesangial cells disrupted the glomerular capillary tufts formation, leading to dysplastic glomeruli, proteinuria, oliguria, reduced looping of glomerular capillaries and capillary dilation. Drosha knockdown in mesangial cells (SV40 MES 13) leads to decreased cell proliferation and reduced Gata3 protein level. Transcriptome analysis by RNA-seq shows decreased levels of ribosomal protein genes (RPGs) but unaltered mRNA levels of major genes affecting kidney development, including Gata3, Pax2, Atn1, Wt1 etc., in Drosha-KD compared to Control SV40 MES13 cells. Further analysis indicates Drosha regulates the translation of Gata3 in mesangial cells via regulating RPG transcription. Removal of Drosha in adult mesangial cells did not cause significant kidney dysfunction, indicating that Drosha functions primarily during development rather than in homeostasis. Our work reveals that Drosha in mesangial cells orchestrates the formation of glomerular capillary tufts by regulating Gata3 translation. It identifies the critical role of DROSHA in nephric development and proposes DROSHA as a novel potential causal gene for congenital anomalies of the kidney and the urinary tract (CAKUT).

title: Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation targeting bilateral primary motor cortex: Promotion of corticospinal remodeling and motor recovery after incomplete spinal cord injury.
abstract: Functional recovery after incomplete spinal cord injury remains limited largely because injured corticospinal pathways have insufficient capacity for structural remodeling and reconnection. Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation targeting the primary motor cortex (M1) can modulate cortical excitability, but whether it drives corticospinal tract remodeling after spinal cord injury and how neurotrophic mechanisms contribute to this process remain poorly understood. Glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factor-related signaling may provide a biological link between cortical stimulation and regenerative responses within the injured nervous system. A multilevel translational design integrating transcriptomic analysis, animal experiments and exploratory clinical evaluation was applied. Public spinal cord injury transcriptomic datasets were integrated to identify shared repair-associated genes and pathways. Bilateral M1-targeted repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation was administered in a T10 incomplete spinal cord injury rat model, with or without systemic anti-glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factor antibody treatment. Behavioral, electrophysiological, histological and molecular analyses were performed to evaluate functional recovery, corticospinal tract remodeling and glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factor-related signaling. Finally, an exploratory randomized controlled trial was conducted to assess functional, electrophysiological and serum biomarker responses to repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation in patients with incomplete spinal cord injury. Integrated transcriptomic analysis identified 51 shared differentially expressed genes linked to neurotrophic regulation, neural remodeling and PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling. In rats with incomplete spinal cord injury, bilateral M1-targeted repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation improved locomotor recovery and corticospinal function, promoted corticospinal tract remodeling, and modulated a glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factor-associated PTEN/PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling profile, whereas anti-glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factor antibody treatment partially attenuated these repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation-associated effects. Spinal RNA sequencing further revealed enrichment of pathways related to axonal growth and synaptic function. Clinically, real repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation was associated with superior functional and electrophysiological outcomes and higher serum levels of neuroplasticity-associated biomarkers than sham stimulation. In summary, bilateral M1-targeted repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation was associated with corticospinal tract remodeling and functional recovery after incomplete spinal cord injury. Preclinical findings support a contributory role of glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factor-associated PTEN/PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling in repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation-induced neural repair, whereas the exploratory clinical results provide preliminary translational evidence without demonstrating the same molecular mechanism in humans.

title: B-cell intrinsic Pax transactivation domain-interacting protein promotes intestinal inflammation by restraining B2 cell-mediated macrophage interleukin-10 responses.
abstract: B cells are increasingly recognized as important regulators of intestinal inflammation through both antibody-dependent and antibody-independent mechanisms, but the intrinsic programs controlling inflammatory B-cell functions remain poorly understood. Pax transactivation domain-interacting protein (PTIP) is an essential regulator of B-cell humoral immunity; however, its role in inflammatory B-cell responses remains unclear. We investigated the function of B-cell-intrinsic PTIP using B-cell-specific PTIP-deficient mice and dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced experimental colitis. Pax transactivation domain-interacting protein expression was evaluated in murine and human B cells, including analysis of a publicly available human colonic single-cell RNA-sequencing dataset. Antibody-mediated effects, B2-cell-intrinsic activity, and macrophage-associated responses were examined using adoptive transfer, serum transfer, macrophage depletion, and interleukin (IL)-10 pathway blockade approaches. PTIP expression was increased in circulating B cells from patients with inflammatory bowel disease and intestinal B cells during DSS-induced colitis. B-cell-specific PTIP deficiency attenuated colitis severity and reduced germinal center B-cell responses and immunoglobulin production. However, adoptive transfer and serum transfer experiments suggested that the protective effect of PTIP deficiency was largely independent of antibody-mediated mechanisms. Transfer of PTIP-deficient conventional B2 cells reduced intestinal inflammation, whereas PTIP-expressing B2 cells promoted disease severity, demonstrating a B2-cell intrinsic function of PTIP. Furthermore, PTIP deficiency enhanced macrophage-associated IL-10 responses, and disruption of macrophage function or IL-10 signaling diminished this protective phenotype. PTIP promotes DSS-induced intestinal inflammation by regulating antibody-independent B2-cell inflammatory activity and B2-cell-macrophage communication. These findings identify a previously unrecognized PTIP-dependent immune regulatory pathway linking B-cell intrinsic programs to macrophage-mediated intestinal inflammation.

title: Comprehensive single-cell RNA sequencing analysis reveals key immune regulators and signaling pathways in people living with HIV across tissues and cell types.
abstract: To identify shared gene signatures, regulatory networks, and shared molecular regulators associated with HIV infection across tissues and cell types using publicly available single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) datasets from people living with HIV. We systematically analyzed human scRNA-seq datasets from brain, cerebrospinal fluid, blood, adipose tissue, and peripheral immune cells from people living with HIV with or without antiretroviral therapy and uninfected controls. HIV-associated genes were identified across datasets, followed by network, transcription factor, and microRNA analyses to identify shared regulatory programs. Findings were evaluated in independent human datasets and validated by immunohistochemistry in brain tissue from simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV)-infected rhesus macaques. Nineteen HIV-associated genes were shared across sample types, including seven hub genes (CD68, TIMP1, AIF1, EGR1, IL1B, MS4A6A, and SPI1). These genes were enriched in immune activation, innate immune systems, and inflammatory pathways. Regulatory network analysis identified SPI1 as a highly connected transcriptional regulator and hsa-miR-155-5p as a prominent microRNA regulator. SPI1 and EGR1 showed increased detection in independent human HIV datasets and increased protein detection in SIV-infected macaque brain tissue. Cross-dataset single-cell transcriptomic analysis identified HIV-associated molecular programs across biological compartments and highlighted SPI1 and EGR1 as candidates and potential regulators of HIV-associated inflammation. These findings provide a framework for further investigation of their roles in HIV-associated complications, including HIV-associated neurocognitive disorders and cardiovascular disease.

title: Sex-Specific Circadian Dysregulation in the Choroid Plexus of a Nitroglycerin Rat Model of Chronic Migraine: An RNA-Seq Analysis.
abstract: Migraine patients show choroid plexus (CP) changes, impairing the blood-CSF barrier. The CP regulates circadian rhythms, but links between CP circadian genes and migraine are unexplored. This study examined changes in the CP circadian gene transcriptome in a chronic migraine rat model compared with controls to identify migraine-related pathways. Chronic migraine model: Sprague-Dawley rats (3 females, 3 males) received nitroglycerin (NTG) every other day for 9 days; controls (3 females, 3 males) got saline. CP from the 4th ventricle was collected 2 hours after the final injection for RNA-seq. Migraine Behavior: Von Frey hair tests on days 1, 5, and 9, pre- and 2 hours post-NTG/saline injection, assessed basal and NTG-induced pain thresholds. RNA-seq & Analysis: Differentially expressed genes (p < 0.05, fold change > 1) were identified. GO, KEGG, and Reactome enrichment analyses were performed to assess changes in circadian gene expression. The NTG group showed reduced basal and NTG-induced pain thresholds on days 1, 5, and 9. Females had a greater number of upregulated genes (MT2A, SLC7A11); males had upregulated ZBTB16 and S100A8. SLC7A11, SCG2, and GRIA1 showed inverse regulation (up in females, down in males). Circadian gene expression altered: 10 genes upregulated (e.g., SERPINE1, MAPK9, ATF4), 13 downregulated (e.g., PER2, DBP, EZH2). Sex-specific differences: females (FBXL12, GPR157), males (NKX2-1, ATF4, CLOCK). GO/KEGG analyses revealed significant enrichment of circadian rhythm-related pathways, insulin resistance, and inflammatory response processes, with sex-specific differences: females showed enrichment in HIF-1 signaling and hemoglobin-related pathways, while males exhibited enrichment in arachidonic acid and leukotriene production. CP transcriptomics in the rat migraine model revealed sex-specific gene regulation, with females upregulating antioxidant genes (MT2A, SLC7A11) and males upregulating inflammatory factors (ZBTB16, S100A8), alongside circadian disruption (e.g., SERPINE1 upregulated, PER2 downregulated). Pathway analyses indicate enriched circadian rhythms, HIF-1 signaling (females), inflammatory processes (males), lipid metabolism (PPARα), and heme signaling, highlighting sex-specific and circadian targets for migraine therapy.

title: Mechanistic investigation of SOCS2-mediated suppression of hepatocellular carcinoma progression via regulation of ferroptosis through the Nrf2/GPX4 signaling axis.
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is one of the most lethal malignancies worldwide and is associated with a poor prognosis. Ferroptosis, a newly recognized form of programmed cell death, plays a critical role in the initiation and progression of HCC. Suppressor of cytokine signaling 2 (SOCS2) has been reported to exert tumor-suppressive functions in various cancers, however, its specific role in HCC and its relationship with ferroptosis remain to be fully elucidated. Integrated bioinformatic analyses of GEO and TCGA datasets were performed using weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) combined with multiple machine learning algorithms to identify key genes associated with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), followed by single-cell RNA sequencing analysis to characterize the tumor microenvironment. Functional experiments were conducted in HCC cells with SOCS2 overexpression or knockdown to assess proliferation, migration, invasion, ferroptosis-related phenotypes, and mitochondrial function. In addition, a nude mouse subcutaneous xenograft model was established to evaluate the role of SOCS2 in vivo. Bioinformatics analysis identified 230 core differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), which were predominantly enriched in pathways related to the cell cycle, ferroptosis, and oxidative phosphorylation. Single-cell analysis revealed that SOCS2, GPX4, and ACSL4 exhibited cell subtype-specific expression patterns across distinct cellular populations. Functional assays demonstrated that SOCS2 overexpression significantly inhibited the proliferation, migration, and invasion of HCC cells, while inducing ferroptosis-related phenotypes characterized by decreased glutathione (GSH) levels, increased malondialdehyde (MDA) and reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, and reduced mitochondrial membrane potential. Notably, these effects were partially reversed by Ferrostatin-1 treatment. Mechanistically, SOCS2 overexpression was accompanied by increased Nrf2 and decreased GPX4 protein levels, and Nrf2 knockdown partially reversed the changes in GPX4 expression and cellular phenotypes. Knockdown of Nrf2 partially restored GPX4 expression and alleviated SOCS2-mediated suppression of cell proliferation as well as oxidative stress. In vivo experiments further confirmed that SOCS2 overexpression markedly inhibited tumor growth, an effect that was partially abrogated by Nrf2 silencing. These results suggest that SOCS2 suppresses HCC cell proliferation and tumor growth in association with ferroptosis-related phenotypes, potentially involving the Nrf2/GPX4 axis. This study provides a preliminary experimental basis for understanding the regulatory network of ferroptosis in HCC and suggests SOCS2 as a candidate molecule for further translational investigation.

title: METTL1 maintains epidermal barrier integrity and limits psoriasiform inflammation, in part through stabilization of p63 mRNA.
abstract: Psoriasis reflects a pathological coupling of epidermal barrier dysfunction and immune activation. However, the keratinocyte-intrinsic mechanisms that maintain epidermal homeostasis and restrain inflammation remain incompletely understood. To investigate the role of METTL1 in epidermal homeostasis and psoriasiform inflammation. Public bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing datasets were analyzed to assess METTL1 expression in psoriatic skin. METTL1 was knocked down in primary human epidermal stem and progenitor cells (EPSCs) and organotypic epidermis. We assess proliferation, apoptosis, RT-qPCR, RNA immunoprecipitation, mRNA stability and p63 rescue. Epidermal-specific Mettl1 knockout mice challenged with imiquimod (IMQ) were used for in vivo validation. Overall METTL1 expression was increased in human psoriatic epidermis and dynamically correlated with disease activity, although METTL1 expression per positive keratinocyte was decreased. METTL1 knockdown impaired EPSCs proliferation and self-renewal while inducing a psoriasis-like inflammatory transcriptional program that overlapped significantly with the human psoriasis transcriptome. METTL1 stabilized TP63 mRNA and maintained p63 protein levels, and enforced p63 expression partially rescued the proliferative defect. In vivo, epidermal Mettl1 deletion caused early impairment of proliferation and barrier gene expression programs with heightened neutrophilic inflammation, followed by exaggerated hyperplasia and delayed resolution of IMQ-induced inflammation. METTL1 is a keratinocyte-intrinsic safeguard of epidermal homeostasis. It supports EPSC proliferative capacity, in part by stabilizing TP63 mRNA, and its loss is associated with impaired barrier programs and heightened inflammation. These findings suggest that keratinocyte-intrinsic RNA regulation influences barrier integrity and the persistence of inflammation in psoriasis.

title: EOMES high PD-1 high CD103 + effector memory CD8 T cells in malignant pleural effusion: a distinct subset implicated in anti-tumor immunity and immunotherapeutic response.
abstract: Malignant pleural effusion (MPE) is a frequent complication of advanced cancers and is associated with poor prognosis, including in patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). We characterized T-cell populations in pleural effusion samples from patients with malignant (n = 34) and benign (n = 11) conditions using multiparametric flow cytometry and cytokine analysis, complemented by reanalysis of publicly available single-cell RNA sequencing datasets. MPE was characterized by enrichment of CD8⁺ effector memory (EM) T cells, including a distinct EOMEShighPD-1highCD103+ population. This subset exhibited increased expression of tissue residency-associated markers, including CD69 and CXCR6, together with increased granzyme B and Ki-67 expression and enhanced IFN-γ production following CD3/CD28 stimulation. Despite high PD-1 expression, it did not exhibit a coordinated increase in exhaustion-associated markers. Single-cell transcriptomic analyzes of breast cancer- and lung adenocarcinoma-associated MPE datasets identified related HLA-II⁺ CD8⁺ T-cell states with effector-associated features, and increased HLA-DR protein expression was confirmed by flow cytometry. Among patients receiving ICIs, this population was more abundant in those showing improvement in malignant pleural effusion, whose overall responses ranged from stable disease to partial response, whereas patients without pleural effusion improvement had progressive disease. These findings identify a tissue residency-associated, HLA-II-expressing CD8⁺ EM T-cell population with effector-associated features in MPE and suggest its potential clinical relevance during ICI therapy.

title: Identification of Immune-Associated Hub Genes Related to the G2/M Checkpoint Pathway in Bladder Cancer Through Integrated Bioinformatics Analysis.
abstract: Bladder cancer is a highly heterogeneous malignancy characterized by complex immune interactions that influence disease progression and patient outcomes. Identifying immune-related molecular determinants with prognostic and therapeutic relevance is therefore critical. This study aimed to systematically investigate immune-related genes involved in bladder cancer and to identify key predictive molecular prognostic biomarkers, with particular emphasis on cell-cycle-associated immune mechanisms. RNA expression profiles from bladder tumor and corresponding normal tissues were analyzed across five independent cohorts (GSE13507, GSE19915, GSE40355, GSE42089, and TCGA-Bladder Cancer). Common differentially expressed immune-related genes (DEIRGs) were identified using GEO2R and TCGA analyses. Functional enrichment and pathway analyses were performed using Metascape and DAVID, while hub genes were identified through protein-protein interaction networks using MCODE, CytoHubba, and ClueGO. Expression patterns, prognostic relevance, and immune associations were validated using UALCAN, the Human Protein Atlas, TIMER2.0, and PrognoScan databases. A total of 300 common DEIRGs were identified across datasets. Network analysis revealed 21 significant immune-related hub genes, several of which were consistently enriched in the G2M checkpoint pathway. Eleven hub genes were significantly associated with reduced overall survival in bladder cancer patients. Notably, six G2M checkpoint-related genes (TOP2A, CCNA2, CDK1, BIRC5, PLK1, and E2F1) demonstrated strong prognostic relevance across multiple cohorts. This comprehensive in silico analysis highlights the critical role of G2M checkpoint-associated immune-related genes in bladder cancer progression. These genes represent predictive molecular prognostic immune biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets, providing a foundation for the development of personalized immunotherapeutic strategies in bladder cancer.

title: Combination of Radiation Treatment and PLK4-Inhibitor, CFI-400945, Leads to Upregulation of ICAM-1, STAT3 Activation, and Cellular Senescence in TNBC.
abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is one of the most aggressive and highly metastatic subtypes of breast cancer. It lacks canonical biomarkers and is often resistant to treatments, including radiotherapy (RT). This mandates the development of better treatments through identifying novel therapeutic targets and biomarkers in TNBC to improve patient stratification for treatment and facilitate novel drug development. We have previously shown that anticancer effects of RT are synergized by the inhibition of polo-like kinase 4 (PLK4) by CFI-400945. In the present study, we aimed to obtain mechanistic insights of the anticancer effects of RT in combination with CFI-400945 using bulk RNA-sequencing in MDA-MB-231 TNBC cells treated with single agents and their combination. Differential gene expression (DEG) and pathway enrichment analyses of the bulk transcriptomics data have identified perturbations in immune and senescence related genes and pathways in TNBC cells treated with RT alone or in combination with CFI-400945. Validation of the identified DEGs showed significant upregulation of ICAM-1 (Intercellular Adhesion Molecule-1) both at transcript and protein levels following combination treatment compared to untreated control cells. This was accompanied by activation of STAT3 protein and increased cellular senescence determined by β-galactosidase assay in combination treatment compared to untreated control. Overall, our data suggest that ICAM-1 and STAT3 signaling axis may play an important role in TNBC cell response to RT and PLK4 inhibition.

title: Integrated Multi-Omics and Machine Learning for Prioritizing Candidate Plasma Proteins in Alzheimer's Disease and Predicting Multi-Target Interactions of Traditional Chinese Medicine.
abstract: This study integrated multi-omics data and machine learning to prioritize candidate plasma proteins and to predict the multi-target interactions of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Mendelian randomization across three cohorts (Icelandic, UK Biobank, and Fenland) identified 66 AD-associated plasma proteins, including TREM2, ACE, GRN, and CR1, with TREM2 showing a robust protective effect (OR = 0.78, 95% CI: 0.75-0.81). Single-cell RNA sequencing showed neuron-specific downregulation of NSF and TMEM106B in AD, implicating synaptic dysfunction and impaired axonal transport. A machine-learning classifier (K-nearest neighbors, KNN) incorporating TREM2, TMEM106B, C1S, PLOD2, and NSF, trained on brain-tissue expression data, demonstrated moderate predictive performance (AUC = 0.76, 95% CI: 0.63-0.90) and is presented as a candidate brain-tissue-derived classifier rather than a validated non-invasive plasma diagnostic panel. Immune infiltration analysis revealed altered M2 macrophage and plasma cell dynamics, with NSF negatively correlated with γδ T-cell infiltration (p < 0.001). Network pharmacology prioritized five candidate TCM herbs (e.g., Scutellaria baicalensis [Huang Qin] and Alpinia oxyphylla [Yi Zhi]) and bioactive compounds (stigmasterol and quercetin) targeting AD-related proteins. Molecular docking predicted strong binding between stigmasterol and PLOD2 (binding energy: -11.2kcal/mol), suggesting a potential role in modulating extracellular matrix remodeling. These compounds were enriched in the PI3K-Akt and NF-κB pathways, consistent with the anti-inflammatory effects observed in TCM formulations such as GHYSJ. These findings link candidate biomarker discovery with the predicted multi-target interactions of TCM, providing hypotheses for future non-invasive diagnosis and precision therapy in AD.

title: Systematic Characterization of Clinically Actionable Antibody-Drug Targets Across Solid Tumors to Advance Precision Oncology.
abstract: The rapid expansion of antibody therapeutics is shifting the clinical bottleneck from drug availability to precise patient selection. We systematically characterize 87 clinically actionable tumor-associated antigens across solid tumors by integrating transcriptomic, proteomic, spatial, and single-cell profiles from more than 32,000 specimens to define expression prevalence, intratumoral heterogeneity, immune contexture, internalization and payload-sensitivity pathways, and translational relevance. We establish ANCHOR, a coordinate reference framework for standardizing patient RNA-seq data, and develop ReSort, a two-tiered scoring system for scalable target prioritization. ReSort enables virtual basket and umbrella trial matching, demonstrates concordance with clinical assays, predicts therapeutic response in patient-derived models, and identifies repurposing opportunities in rare malignancies. We develop an AI-based decision-support agent for antibody trial matching and construct a multimodal feature space integrating tumor- and protein-intrinsic attributes to guide systematic target discovery and prioritization. This work provides a scalable, clinically actionable approach for precision antibody-based therapies and next-generation target development.

title: Loss of LKB1 is Associated with Cisplatin Resistance in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma and Pharmacological Activation of the LKB1-AMPK Axis Attenuates the Resistant Phenotype.
abstract: Cisplatin resistance remains a major clinical obstacle in the treatment of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), highlighting the urgent need for novel therapeutic strategies. The tumor suppressor LKB1 and its downstream effector AMPK are known to regulate cancer progression and chemoresistance. LKB1-AMPK signaling is a master negative regulator of mTOR and cellular metabolism, and its loss has been linked to chemoresistance; however, the specific roles of this axis in cisplatin-resistant OSCC are not fully understood. This study aimed to investigate whether pharmacological activation of the LKB1-AMPK axis can attenuate the cisplatin-resistant phenotype in oral carcinoma cells. We assessed LKB1 expression in cisplatin-resistant HSC-3 cells and evaluated the effects of the LKB1 activators honokiol and metformin on cell growth. siRNA-mediated knockdown of PRKAA1 (AMPKα1) was used to test whether AMPK is required for the effects of honokiol. Our findings were further examined in a three-dimensional (3D) spheroid model and complemented by supportive transcriptomic analysis using publicly available single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data from human OSCC samples. LKB1 mRNA and protein were significantly reduced in cisplatin-resistant HSC-3 cells compared with parental cells (mRNA: ~0.35-fold, p < 0.01; protein: ~0.50-fold, p < 0.01). Honokiol and metformin dose-dependently increased p-LKB1 (up to ~3.5-fold and ~4.0-fold at 50 μM, respectively), suppressed cell viability and migration, and induced apoptosis; siRNA-mediated AMPK knockdown reduced honokiol-induced apoptosis by approximately 50-60% (p < 0.01). In 3D spheroids, both agents reduced viability in a dose-dependent manner. Supportive scRNA-seq analysis of human OSCC samples showed that low STK11 expression in malignant cells was associated with reduced transcriptional scores of AMPK downstream targets and enrichment of mTOR and cisplatin-resistance signatures. Pharmacological activation of the LKB1-AMPK axis by honokiol or metformin attenuates the cisplatin-resistant phenotype in oral carcinoma cells in an AMPK-dependent manner. These findings support further investigation of LKB1-AMPK-targeted strategies, while in vivo resensitization experiments remain necessary.

title: Targeting MAP1A overcomes immunotherapy resistance in triple-negative breast cancer by restoring tumor antigen presentation via JAK1-STAT1 inhibition.
abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have demonstrated clinical benefit in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), yet primary resistance remains a major therapeutic obstacle. Transcriptomic profiles were integrated with clinical response data from immunotherapy cohorts to identify candidate regulators of resistance. The biological functions of candidate genes were investigated using in vitro and in vivo models, including syngeneic mouse models and genetic knockout approaches. Mechanistic studies were conducted using RNA sequencing, flow cytometry, co-immunoprecipitation, and protein stability assays. Microtubule-associated protein 1A (MAP1A) expression was significantly upregulated in patients with anti-PD-1 resistance. Functionally, MAP1A promoted an immunologically cold tumor microenvironment and conferred resistance to anti-PD-1 therapy in murine models. Mechanistically, MAP1A interacted with JAK1 and contributed to the regulation of its ubiquitination and degradation, thereby suppressing STAT1 phosphorylation and the transcription of major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC-I) and antigen presentation machinery (APM) genes. Upstream, MAP1A expression was transcriptionally upregulated by the TGF-β/SMAD3 signaling pathway. Therapeutic inhibition of TGF-β signaling with galunisertib enhanced MHC-I-related antigen presentation programs and sensitized MAP1A-high tumors to anti-PD-1 therapy in vivo. Our work delineates the TGF-β/MAP1A/MHC-I axis as an immune evasion pathway and supports MAP1A as a candidate response-associated biomarker warranting prospective evaluation. These findings also provide a preclinical rationale for targeting TGF-β to enhance immunotherapy in MAP1A-high TNBCs. Major funding was provided by the National Natural Science Foundation of China.

title: Deep learning-based integrative single-cell transcriptomic analysis of vitiligo.
abstract: Vitiligo is an immune-mediated depigmentation disorder in which interferon-γ signalling and autoreactive CD8+ T cells are central, but the cross-cohort cellular ecosystem and donor-level disease signature remain incompletely resolved. We conducted a retrospective analysis of three public skin single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets comprising 35 donors and 93,287 post-quality-control cells. We combined donor-aware cell-composition and pseudobulk analyses with a deep attention multiple-instance learning model, and reserved a separate balanced patient -control cohort for independent evaluation. Eleven major cell populations were identified. The donor-level classifier achieved 0.914 accuracy and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.990 in donor-stratified five-fold cross-validation. After Benjamini -Hochberg correction across 11 cell types, vitiligo lesions showed macrophage expansion and depletion of fibroblasts, endothelial cells, and mast cells (all q = 0.029). Integrated ranking prioritised an interferon-γ/CXCL9 -CXCL10 programme, while CD8+ T cells displayed Trm-associated and cytotoxic-effector transcriptional states. An eight-feature signature trained only in the primary discovery cohort achieved an area under the curve of 0.944 (95% CI, 0.778 -1.000) and accuracy of 0.750 (95% CI, 0.468 -0.911) in a small independent cohort of six healthy controls and six patients with vitiligo; exact label permutation supported discrimination (p = 0.003). A directional omnibus test across ten prespecified validation measures supported panel-level concordance (p = 0.023), although no individual measure remained significant after multiple-testing correction. These findings provide preliminary external support for a multivariable signal connecting an expanded macrophage compartment, interferon-associated chemokine signalling, and Trm-like CD8+ T-cell states.

title: TRIM56 stabilizes FMRP by reducing its ubiquitination to activate MAPK/ERK signaling and drive osteosarcoma progression.
abstract: Osteosarcoma (OS) is the most prevalent primary malignant bone tumor in children and adolescents, characterized by high metastatic propensity and dismal prognosis. Although post-translational modifications are established as critical regulators of oncogenic signaling in OS, the precise molecular machinery governing these processes remains poorly defined. Expression of TRIM56 was assessed via public datasets (TCGA/GEO/CCLE) and IHC on tissue arrays, with scRNA-seq utilized to infer its functional context. In vitro, TRIM56 modulation affected proliferation (CCK-8/EdU) and migration (Transwell/Wound Healing), while Co-IP, IF, and ubiquitination assays confirmed TRIM56-FMRP interaction. CHX chase and MG132 treatment revealed TRIM56-mediated stabilization of FMRP. TRIM56 activated the MAPK/ERK signaling pathway (validated by Western blotting and rescue assays), and its oncogenicity was corroborated in vivo using a subcutaneous xenograft model. TRIM56 was markedly upregulated in OS tissues and functionally drove proliferation and migration, effects rescued by its knockdown. Single-cell RNA sequencing mapped high TRIM56 expression predominantly to endothelial cells and CD8+ T cells. Integrative RNA-seq analysis linked TRIM56 to MAPK/ERK signaling; correspondingly, TRIM56 overexpression elevated p-MEK/MEK and p-ERK/ERK ratios, while TRIM56 depletion suppressed them. Crucially, pharmacological inhibition with PD98059 reversed TRIM56-induced hyperactivation of this pathway, confirming a genetic epistasis. Mechanistically, Co-immunoprecipitation and immunofluorescence assays confirmed the physical interaction and colocalization between TRIM56 and FMRP. Ubiquitination assays and cycloheximide (CHX) chase experiments demonstrated that TRIM56 attenuated the polyubiquitination of FMRP and prolonged its protein half-life. Consistent with these findings, subcutaneous xenograft models revealed that TRIM56 promoted the in vivo proliferative capacity of OS cells. This research identifies a novel TRIM56-FMRP-MAPK/ERK axis driving OS via post-translational modification, positioning TRIM56 as a promising therapeutic target for precision oncology.

title: Multicenter CT-Based Deep Learning for Preoperative Nodal Risk Stratification in Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma.
abstract: Accurate preoperative risk stratification for lymph node metastasis (LNM) in papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) remains difficult. We developed and validated ThyLNT, a Transformer-based 2.5D deep learning model using preoperative computed tomography (CT), and explored related biological features in multi-omics analyses. A total of 1560 patients with PTC from six hospitals were retrospectively included. The Tongji Hospital cohort was divided into training and internal validation sets, and five external cohorts were used for independent testing. Seven 2.5D tumor slices were extracted per patient, encoded with a DenseNet201 backbone, and fused by a Transformer. Model performance was compared with radiomics, ensemble learning, and multi-instance learning using AUC, calibration, decision curve, and precision-recall analyses. Bulk RNA-seq, single-cell RNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics, and spatial metabolomics were used to explore related biological features. ThyLNT achieved an AUC of 0.882 (CI, 0.858-0.905) in the training cohort, 0.787 (CI, 0.738-0.835) in the internal validation cohort, and 0.772 (CI, 0.662-0.878) to 0.827 (CI, 0.763-0.885) across the five external cohorts. It showed multicenter discrimination, whereas calibration and threshold-dependent operating characteristics varied across cohorts. Multi-omics analyses provided exploratory biological context, including candidate associations with vascular endothelial growth factor A-related signaling and lipid metabolism. ThyLNT demonstrated multicenter performance for preoperative LNM prediction in PTC and may support risk stratification, although calibration, threshold use, and clinical utility require prospective validation.

title: Transcriptomic Evaluation of SFTPD Expression in COPD Lung Tissue Using RNA-Seq.
abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Surfactant protein D (SP-D), encoded by the SFTPD gene, has been strongly implicated in COPD through genetic associations, protein-level biomarkers, and functional studies. However, whether SFTPD is dysregulated at the transcriptomic level in lung tissue remains unclear. To evaluate whether SFTPD is transcriptionally dysregulated in COPD lung tissue. Retrospective transcriptomic analysis of publicly available RNA-seq data. We re-analyzed publicly available RNA-seq data from lung tissue samples (BioProject: PRJNA1151128) comprising COPD patients (n = 9) and control subjects (n = 9) using a reproducible bioinformatics workflow (HISAT2, StringTie, edgeR with FDR correction). In addition to differential expression testing, we calculated effect sizes and performed post-hoc power analysis to rigorously assess the robustness of null findings. Furthermore, findings were validated using an independent microarray dataset (GSE47460). Overall, 114 genes were upregulated and 104 were downregulated in COPD lung tissue compared with controls. In contrast, SFTPD expression was not significantly differentially expressed (log2FC = 0.316; FDR = 0.421). The effect size was small (Cohen's d = 0.42), and power analysis indicated 23% sensitivity to detect the observed fold change, though 80% power was achieved for ≥2.1-fold changes. This study evaluated whether SFTPD is transcriptionally dysregulated in COPD lung tissue using RNA-seq data and demonstrates that SFTPD mRNA levels are not significantly altered. These findings suggest that COPD-associated alterations in SP-D arise through post-transcriptional or systemic mechanisms rather than lung tissue transcription. These findings were further supported by external validation using a large public lung tissue dataset. By rigorously validating and reporting a null result, this work reduces publication bias, informs biomarker strategies, and highlights the need for integrative single-cell and multi-omics approaches to clarify SP-D regulation in COPD.

title: SPATS2 triggers immune evasion and anti-PD-1 resistance of hepatocellular carcinoma by inducing dendritic cell phagocytic dysfunction.
abstract: The clinical efficacy of anti-PD-1 immunotherapy in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains limited due to the inherently immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. This study aims to investigate the role of the spermatogenesis-associated serine-rich protein 2 (SPATS2) in mediating resistance to anti-PD-1 immunotherapy in HCC. Five independent HCC anti-PD-1 therapy RNA-seq cohorts (n = 105) were included to identify key genes driving anti-PD-1 resistance. Multiplex immunofluorescence staining, single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptome analysis, flow cytometry, in vitro co-culture systems, RNA immunoprecipitation assays, mice spontaneous HCC models and patient-derived organoid models to elucidate the biological function of SPATS2 in tumor progression and immune escape. Cross-cohort analysis identified SPATS2 as a critical driver of anti-PD-1 resistance in HCC. Elevated SPATS2 expression promotes immune evasion by impairing dendritic cell (DC) infiltration and phagocytic activity, leading to therapeutic resistance. Mechanistically, SPATS2 binds AU-rich elements (ARE) in the CD47 3'UTR to stabilize its mRNA and interacts with the eIF4F complex. These two interactions result in CD47 mRNA circularization, and facilitate recruitment of translation initiation factors to the translation start site, thereby enhancing CD47 translation. Increased CD47 suppresses DC uptake of tumor-derived mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA), thereby dampening DC cGAS-STING signaling and subsequently CD8⁺ T cell-mediated antitumor responses. Importantly, targeted silencing of SPATS2 via lipid nanoparticle-delivered siRNA, or combination with anti-CD47 therapy, significantly improved HCC anti-PD-1 therapeutic efficacy. SPATS2 facilitates immune evasion and anti-PD-1 resistance in HCC by inhibiting DC infiltration and impairing phagocytic function. Targeting SPATS2 or combining with anti-CD47 monoclonal antibody strategy is expected to overcome immunotherapy tolerance and improve the immune response rate of HCC patients.

title: ITGB2 has potential as a prognostic factor for the immune microenvironment of gastric cancer tumours and as an indicator of tumour microenvironment remodelling.
abstract: In recent years, correlation studies of immune infiltration in gastric cancers, such as STAD have attracted much attention. However, the correlation between the expression of the immune factor ITGB2 and the malignant features of immune infiltration and gastric cancer has rarely been reported. Batch RNA-seq and scRNA-seq data were combined to screen for differentially expressed genes using software packages and machine learning. Data from the TCGA and five GEO databases were used to investigate the expression levels of ITGB2 in patients with STAD, and the correlation between ITGB2 expression levels and gastric cancer progression was explored and validated. The expression of ITGB2 was validated through rt-qPCR and Western blot analysis in cell experiments. Several algorithms were used to analyse the correlation between ITGB2 and immune infiltration in patients with STAD. The study predicted chemotherapy and immunotherapy responses for subgroups with high and low expression of ITGB2. Gene knockdown was performed on gastric cancer cells to confirm its correlation with immune checkpoint ligand-related genes and conduct preliminary validation of its signaling pathways. Furthermore, migration, invasion, and proliferative abilities were assessed using the Transwell assay and CCK-8 assay. This study revealed that ITGB2 is significantly elevated in gastric cancer, while increased levels of ITGB2 were linked to worse clinical outcomes and prognosis in STAD patients. Lower expression levels of PD-L1 were observed concurrently in the ITGB2 knockdown group. Moreover, gastric cancer patients with high levels of ITGB2 had better responses to immunotherapy. Finally, prognostic features using LASSO regression demonstrated satisfactory prognostic predictive ability. ITGB2 expression is a promising potential immune-related biomarker for STAD, and the prognostic model and immunotherapy sensitivity prediction based on ITGB2 may offer new strategies for individualized treatment and may aid in identifying patients who may benefit from immunotherapy, although further clinical validation is warranted.

title: Transcriptomic prognostic modeling reveals limited incremental value of self-reported race and identifies GDPD2 as a candidate prognostic biomarker in lung adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Outcomes in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) differ between White and Black patients, but whether self-reported race carries prognostic information beyond tumor biology remains unclear. Using RNA-sequencing and clinical data from the TCGA-LUAD cohort (440 patients; 388 White, 52 Black), we combined genome-wide survival screening, LASSO-penalized Cox regression, and race-associated differential expression analysis to test whether race adds prognostic value to transcriptomic and clinical variables and to nominate candidate genes. Feature-selection optimism was quantified by repeating screening and LASSO within each training fold of repeated 10-fold cross-validation, with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals. The lead candidate was evaluated in the Kaplan-Meier Plotter lung cancer database. Screening of 59,427 transcripts identified 2737 survival-associated genes, which LASSO reduced to a 124-gene signature. Its apparent C-index of 0.898 fell to 0.618 (95% CI 0.573-0.664) under nested validation, indicating substantial optimism. Adding race did not improve random survival forest performance (nested ΔC-index 0.0008, 95% CI -0.0018 to 0.0035), and race was not significant in any multivariable Cox model, although the small Black subgroup limits precision. Intersecting the signature with 5039 race-associated genes yielded eight candidates, of which GDPD2 was the only protein-coding gene with a reproducible survival association. High GDPD2 expression was associated with poorer survival after adjustment for age, sex, race, and tumor stage in TCGA (HR = 1.31, P=0.004) and in an external cohort of 1161 patients (HR = 1.57, 95% CI 1.32-1.87). In TCGA, GDPD2-high tumors showed extensive transcriptomic differences, enrichment of xenobiotic, lipid, and epithelial-differentiation pathways, and modestly higher estimated B-cell, NK-cell, and dendritic-cell infiltration (Spearman ρ=0.12-0.23). In this cohort, self-reported race added no detectable prognostic information to transcriptomic and clinical variables, although the apparent performance of the signature was optimistic. GDPD2 is a candidate prognostic biomarker with an externally supported survival association; its pathway and immune correlates are exploratory single-cohort findings, and clinical utility is not established.

title: Single-cell analysis identifies a proliferative osteoblastic subpopulation and machine learning-derived prognostic signatures in osteosarcoma.
abstract: Osteosarcoma (OS) shows marked cellular heterogeneity, and patients often have very different clinical outcomes despite similar clinicopathological features. This variability remains difficult to explain using conventional risk factors alone. Here, we combined single-cell transcriptomic analysis, bulk transcriptomic profiling and machine-learning modeling to identify prognostic signatures related to tumor proliferation and the immune microenvironment. Single-cell RNA sequencing data from GSE152048 (n = 11) were used to map the cellular composition of OS. Within the osteoblastic compartment, we identified a proliferative subpopulation enriched for chromosome segregation, mitotic division and microtubule-related processes. We then used the TCGA-SARC cohort (n = 261) for model development and the GSE39058 osteosarcoma cohort (n = 41) for external validation. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis, differential expression analysis and univariate Cox regression were used to screen genes associated with immune features, proliferative activity and prognosis. These genes were defined as immune-proliferation-related signatures (IPRS). Among 117 machine-learning models, the random survival forest model performed best overall, with a 10-fold cross-validated C-index of 0.755 in the TCGA training cohort, an external validation C-index of 0.782 in GSE39058 and an average C-index of 0.769. The IPRS score separated patients into distinct prognostic groups and remained independently associated with overall survival in multivariate Cox analysis. It was also related to immune and stromal scores, immune-cell infiltration patterns and predicted drug sensitivity. We further selected ALG6 for experimental validation. Knockdown of ALG6 reduced proliferation and colony formation and increased apoptosis in 143B and U2OS cells. Overall, these results support the prognostic relevance of IPRS in osteosarcoma and suggest that ALG6 warrants further mechanistic investigation.
